One day, the Queen Mother set up a grand banquet, opening the Treasure Pavilion, hosting a "Peaches Exaltation Gathering" on the Dragon Pool. The seven fairies, dressed in red, white, green, purple, blue, yellow, and yellow-green, respectively, all carried flower baskets and came to the Peaches Garden to pick peaches for the gathering. The seven fairies stood before the garden gate, where they saw the Peaches Garden Guardian, the Strongman, and the heavenly official from the Office of Heaven, all waiting by the gate. The fairy approached and said, "We have been sent by the Queen Mother to fetch peaches for a banquet." The Peaches Garden Guardian said, "Fairy, wait for a moment. This year is not like past years. The Jade Emperor has sent the Heavenly General to oversee the garden, and we cannot let him be unaware of it. We will only open the garden if he has given his approval." The fairy replied, "Where is the Heavenly General?" The Peaches Garden Guardian said, "He is inside the garden, tired and taking a nap on a pavilion." The fairy said, "Very well, let's go and find him. We cannot delay." The Peaches Garden Guardian and the official went together to the pavilion, but only saw the Heavenly General's clothes and hat on the pavilion, but no one was there. They searched in all directions but couldn't find him anywhere. It turned out that the Heavenly General had taken a break, eaten a few peaches, and then transformed into a two-inch tall person who had fallen asleep under the thick leaves at the top of a big tree. The seven fairies said, "We have come on a mission, but we couldn't find the Heavenly General, so we can't leave without reporting back." A nearby heavenly official said, "Fairy, since you have been sent on a mission, you don't need to hesitate. The Heavenly General often takes leisurely strolls, and I'm guessing he's gone to visit friends outside the garden. Why don't you and the others go pick peaches and I'll take care of sending a message back for you." The fairy followed the official's suggestion, going into the woods to pick peaches. She picked two baskets from the first tree and three baskets from the second tree. When she came to the third tree, she only saw a few withered peach pits. It turned out that the ripe ones had been eaten by the Monkey King. The fairy looked around and only saw a half-red and half-white peach on the south branch. The blue-clad fairy pulled down the branch, and the red-clad fairy picked the peach, but then she threw the branch back up. It turned out that the Heavenly General had been hiding there and was startled awake. The Heavenly General then appeared in his true form, pulling out his golden hoop rod from his ear and shouting loudly, "What kind of monster are you, daring to pick my peaches?" The seven fairies all knelt down in fright and said, "Great General, please calm down. We are not evil spirits, but the seven fairies sent by the Queen Mother to fetch peaches for a grand banquet in the Treasure Pavilion. We were told to find you, but we couldn't find you, so we picked some peaches in anticipation of the Queen Mother's order. We hope you can forgive us." The Heavenly General listened and his anger turned to joy. "Rise, fairies. The Queen Mother is hosting a banquet in the Treasure Pavilion. Who is she inviting?" The fairy replied, "As for the guest list, there are the usual protocol. She's inviting the Buddha of the West, bodhisattvas, arhats, the Avalokiteshvara of the South Pole, the Emperor of the Eastern Cultivation, the sages from the Ten Islands, the spirit of the Northern Dipper, the spirit of the Central Pole, and the great sages from the five directions. There's also the Five Star Emissaries, the deities from the Eight Realms, the Eight Trigrams, the Emperor of Heaven, the Eight Yang, and the Eight Yin. There's also the gods from the Three Realms, the ghosts of the underworld, and the deities of the lands. All of them will attend the grand gathering at the Peaches Garden." The Heavenly General laughed and said, "Can I be invited too?" The fairy replied, "We haven't received any word." The Heavenly General said, "I'm the Heavenly General, why can't I be invited? Why not make old Sun Wukong a guest of honor?" The fairy said, "This is a set rule for the grand gathering, I don't know what to do." The Heavenly General said, "You're right, no wonder you're uncertain. Why don't you wait and let me go find out what's going on, see if I can be invited or not?"

One day, the Queen Mother held a banquet, opening the Jade Hall and holding a grand feast at the Peach Orchard, also known as the Peach Gathering. The seven maidens dressed in red, white, purple, yellow, green, black, and pink robes, each carrying a flower basket, went to the Peach Orchard to pick peaches for the banquet. The seven maidens stopped in front of the orchard's gate and saw the orchard's spirit, the guards, and the heavenly officials from the Heavenly Capital, all gathered there, barring the gate. The maidens approached and said, "We have been commissioned by the Queen Mother to come here to pick peaches for the banquet."

The spirit said, "You maids, wait a moment. This year is different from the previous years. The Jade Emperor has appointed the Heavenly General to be in charge here. We must report to the Heavenly General before opening the orchard." The maids asked, "Where is the Heavenly General?" The spirit replied, "The Heavenly General is inside the orchard, resting in a pavilion. He is exhausted, so he is taking a nap." The maids said, "Since it's like that, we must go find him so we don't keep the Queen Mother waiting." The spirit and the guards went with them to find the Heavenly General.

They searched until they reached the Flower Pavilion but saw only the Heavenly General's clothes, with no sign of him. They searched all around, but couldn't find him anywhere. It turned out the Heavenly General had been playing around for a while, eating a few peaches and then transforming into a two-inch tall human, who was sleeping under a thick leaf at the top of a tree.

The seven maids said, "We have been commissioned to come here and can't find the Heavenly General. How can we leave without him?" A nearby heavenly official said, "Maidens, since you have been commissioned, don't be hesitant. The Heavenly General loves to wander and relax, so he might be meeting with friends outside the orchard. You go pick some peaches, and I'll come up with a reason to excuse you." The maids followed the official's suggestion and entered the forest to pick peaches. They picked two baskets from the front tree and three baskets from the middle tree, but when they reached the back tree, they only found a few unripe peaches with green skin. It turned out that the Heavenly General had eaten all the ripe ones. The seven maids looked around and saw only one half-red and half-white peach on the southern branch.

The maids in the green robe pulled the branch down, and the ones in the red robe picked the peach. However, when they put the branch back, they accidentally woke up the Heavenly General, who was sleeping on the branch. The Heavenly General immediately appeared in his true form, pulled out his staff from his ear, and shouted, "Who are you, daring to steal my peaches!" The seven maids immediately knelt down and said, "Great Sage, please forgive us. We are not evil spirits, but the seven maidens commissioned by the Queen Mother to pick peaches for the banquet and hold the Peach Gathering at the Jade Hall."

The Heavenly General heard their explanation and changed his anger to joy, saying, "Maidens, please get up. Who is the Queen Mother inviting to the banquet?" The maids replied, "The usual protocol is for the Western Pure Land Buddha, Bodhisattvas, Arhats, the Bodhisattva of the Southern Pole, the Heavenly Emperor of the East, the sage sages of the ten isles and three islands, the mysterious spirits of the Northern Pole, the Supreme Clear Official of the Central Axis, the five elders from the five directions, the five-star dignitaries, the deities of the eight trigrams and nine palaces, the gods of the eight hells, the king of the earth, and the various deities from the various palaces and temples all to attend the Peach Gathering." The Heavenly General laughed and said, "Can I be invited?" The maids replied, "We haven't received any news about it." The Heavenly General said, "I am the Heavenly General of the Ten Heavens, so why can't I be invited to sit in a dignified position?" The maids said, "This is according to the rules of the gathering. We don't know if it applies this time." The Heavenly General said, "That makes sense. I'll just go find out first and see if I can be invited."

One day, the Queen Mother of the West prepared a grand feast, opening the treasure hall and staging the "Magical Peach Delight" in the Jasper Pool. The seven fairy maidens, wearing red, white, green, blue, purple, yellow, and ochre robes, each carrying a flower basket, came to the Magpie Forest to pick peaches for the feast. The seven fairy maidens approached the entrance of the Magpie Forest, only to see the Forest Spirit and the sturdy men, as well as the two officials of the Heavens' Court, all gathered there, blocking the way. The fairy maiden said, "We are here to comply with the Queen Mother's decree, bringing peaches to the feast." The Forest Spirit replied, "Please wait. This year is different from past years. The Jade Emperor has sent the Great Sage to oversee everything here. We cannot open the forest without his knowledge." The fairy maiden asked, "Where is the Great Sage?" The Forest Spirit replied, "The Great Sage is inside, taking a nap in a pavilion because he is tired." The fairy maiden said, "Very well, we'll go look for him. We cannot delay." The Forest Spirit and his companions went with them to search. They looked in the pavilion but only saw the Great Sage's hat and crown lying there, with no sign of him anywhere else. After searching every corner, they couldn't find him. It turned out that the Great Sage had been playing around, eating a few peaches and transforming himself into a small child of two inches tall, sleeping under the dense leaves at the top of a tall tree. The seven fairy maidens said, "We have come on the Queen Mother's orders, but we can't find the Great Sage. We dare not leave without him." A nearby official whispered, "The fairy maidens are here to comply with the Queen Mother's orders. They don't have to be uncertain. The Great Sage is accustomed to taking leisurely strolls and might have gone out to visit friends. Why don't you ladies just pick some peaches while we send a message for the Great Sage?" The fairy maidens followed his suggestion and entered the tree grove to pick peaches. She first picked two baskets from the front tree, then three from the middle tree, and when she reached the back tree, she saw that the branches were sparse, with only a few unripe peaches left. It turned out that all the ripe ones had been eaten by the Monkey King. The seven fairy maidens looked around, only to see that on the southern branch, there was a single peach that was half-red and half-white. The blue-robed fairy gently pulled on the branch, while the red-robed fairy picked the peach. But as soon as the branch was put back, the Monkey King was awakened from his sleep. The Monkey King immediately transformed back to his original form, pulled out his golden hoop staff, and exclaimed, "Who is that strange creature, daring to steal my peaches?" The seven fairy maidens, frightened, knelt down together and said, "Great Sage, please pardon us. We are not evil spirits but the seven fairy maidens sent by the Queen Mother to bring peaches for the feast, staging the 'Magical Peach Delight'. We came here first to see the Forest Spirit and others, but we couldn't find you. We feared that we would be late for the Queen Mother's orders, so we decided to pick some peaches first. We beg for your pardon." The Monkey King, hearing this, changed from being angry to being pleased, and said, "Rise, fairy maidens. Who is invited to the feast?" The fairy maidens replied, "As usual, we invite the Buddha from the West, the Bodhisattva, the Arhats, the Goddess of Mercy from the South Pole, the Holy Emperor from the East, the wise sages from the Ten Islands, the wise sages from the three islands, the spiritual masters from the North Pole, and the wise sages from the Central Pole. We also invite the five planets, the eight Celestial Masters, the four Emperors, the Heavenly Immortal, the various deities from the eight palaces and the nine courts, the gods from the eight hells, and the Lord of the underworld. All the deities from the various palaces and halls will attend the 'Magical Peach Feast'." The Monkey King laughed and said, "May I be invited?" The fairy maidens replied, "We haven't heard anything about it." The Monkey King said, "I am the Great Sage of Heaven, so why can't I be invited? Can I be seated at a special table?" The fairy maidens said, "This is the usual rule of the feast. We don't know how to arrange it." The Monkey King said, "This makes sense. That's why you're uncertain. Wait, let me go and ask for the news first. Let's see if I can be invited or not."

One day, the Queen of Heaven held a feast, and big open the Treasure Hall, where she made the Jade Pool host the "Canton Peach Banquet". She summoned the seven Immortal Maidens in their respective clothes - the Red-clothed Maiden, the Plain-clothed Maiden, the Blue-clothed Maiden, the Ash-colored Maiden, the Purple-clothed Maiden, the Yellow-clothed Maiden, and the Green-clothed Maiden - each carrying a flower basket, to pick peaches for the banquet.

The seven Immortal Maidens came to the Peach Garden entrance. They saw the Jade Palace Land Deity and the Heavenly Strength Deity together with the Heavenly Capital Deity's Two Bureau clerks, standing guard at the entrance. The Immortal Maidens approached and said, "We are here to receive the Queen's command, to fetch peaches for the banquet." The Jade Palace Land Deity said, "Immortals, wait. This year is different from the past years. The Jade Emperor appointed the Heavenly Great Sage to oversee this place, and we must get permission from the Great Sage before we can open the garden." The Immortal Maidens said, "Where is the Great Sage?" The Jade Palace Land Deity said, "The Great Sage is inside the garden, feeling tired, and is sleeping on a pavilion." The Immortal Maidens said, "In that case, let's go find him and not delay." The Jade Palace Land Deity agreed and went with them.

After searching in the flower pavilion, they only saw the Great Sage's clothing, but didn't see him anywhere. They looked around but couldn't find him anywhere. It turned out that the Great Sage had been playing for a while, eating a few peaches, and then changed into a two-inch tall person, and was sleeping under the thick leaves of a big tree. The seven Immortal Maidens said, "We have come at the Queen's command, but we can't find the Great Sage, and it's not right for us to leave without him." A clerk nearby said, "The Immortals have come on the Queen's command, don't be hesitant. The Great Sage often wanders off and meets with friends, he's probably gone to see them. You may as well go pick some peaches, we'll report back to the Great Sage." The Immortal Maidens followed the advice, and went into the trees to pick peaches. They picked two baskets from the front tree, three from the middle tree, but when they reached the back tree, they saw that the tree had sparse flowers and fruits, with only a few unripe green skin peels left. It turned out that the King of Monkeys had eaten all the ripe ones. The seven Immortal Maidens looked around, and only saw a peach on the south branch that was half red and half white. The Blue-clothed Maiden pulled the branch, and the Red-clothed Maiden picked the peach, but put the branch back. It turned out that the Great Sage had changed, and was sleeping right on the branch. The Great Sage suddenly appeared in his true form, pulled out a golden fillet from his ears, and said with a loud voice, "What kind of monster are you, daring to steal my peaches?" The seven Immortal Maidens were frightened, and fell to the ground in unison, saying, "Great Sage, please forgive us. We are not evil spirits, but the Queen's appointed seven Immortal Maidens, sent to fetch peaches to hold the 'Canton Peach Banquet'. We had just arrived at this place, met the garden's deities, but couldn't find the Great Sage. We were worried that we would be late for the Queen's command, so we picked peaches without waiting for the Great Sage. We humbly ask for your pardon."

The Great Sage heard their words, and changed his anger to joy, saying, "Immortals, please rise. Who is the host at this banquet?" The Immortal Maidens replied, "The host is as per the usual rules, inviting the Buddha of the West, the Bodhisattvas, the Arhats, the Avalokiteshvara of the Southern Dipper, the Celestial Emperor of the Eastern Kingdom, the Immortals of the Five Peaks of the Central Kingdom, the Xuanling of the Northern Dipper, the Yellow Yang of the Yellow Springs. These are the five old immortals of the five directions. There are also the Five Star Kings, the three dignitaries of the Eight Palaces, the Four Emperors, the Tae Yi Tianxian, and the various gods from the Eight Palaces, the Nine Lees, the Sea Yu God, and the underworld's Lord of the Taoist Church, and the Geographical Gods. All the dignitaries and gods from the various palaces and halls are coming to the 'Canton Peach Banquet'." The Great Sage laughed and said, "May I also attend?" The Immortal Maidens replied, "We've never heard of it." The Great Sage said, "I am the Heavenly Great Sage, why not let me, the old Sun Wukong, take a seat?" The Immortal Maidens said, "This is according to the rules of the banquet, we don't know how to proceed." The Great Sage said, "This is also understandable, no wonder you are unsure. Please stand by for now, let me go ask around and see if I can be invited."

One day, Empress Wang held a feast, grandly opening the treasure pavilion, and on the Jade Lake stage, a "delicious peach gathering" was held, with seven fairy girls, dressed in red, white, plain, blue, black, purple, and yellow respectively, each carrying a flower basket, to go to the Peach Garden to pick peaches for the gathering. The seven fairy girls reached the entrance of the Peach Garden, only to see the soil spirit and mighty warrior stationed there, accompanied by the two dignitaries of the Heavenly Court, all looking stern. The fairy girl stepped forward and said, "We come at the behest of Empress Wang to pick peaches and hold the banquet." The soil spirit said, "The fairies should wait. The fairy girl said, "Where is the Great Sage?" The soil spirit replied, "The Great Sage is inside the garden, feeling tired, and is sleeping in a pavilion." The fairy girl said, "Since that's the case, go and find him, we can't be late." The soil spirit and the dignitary went together to find him, but only found the empty pavilion and didn't know where he was. In the end, it was found that the Great Sage had played around for a bit, eaten some peaches, and then changed into a two-inch-tall person, who was fast asleep under a thick-leaved tree at the top of a tall tree. The seven fairy girls said, "We were sent on an errand, and yet we can't find the Great Sage, how can we leave?" A nearby official said, "The fairies don't need to hesitate, since they were sent on a mission. The Great Sage is accustomed to taking leisurely strolls, and is probably out meeting friends. After picking two baskets from the first tree, they picked three more from the middle tree; but when they reached the last tree, they only saw that the fruit was sparse, with only a few green skin peels left. It turned out that all the ripe peaches were eaten by the Monkey King. The seven fairy girls looked around and only saw one peach on the south branch, half red and half white. The blue-clad fairy gently pulled down the branch, and the red-clad fairy picked the peach, but then she carelessly dropped the branch upwards. It turned out that the Great Sage had transformed and was actually sleeping on that very branch. The Great Sage immediately revealed his true form, took out his golden hoop staff from his ears, and gave a loud shout, "Who are you, daring to steal my peaches with such audacity?" The seven fairy girls were frightened and knelt down, saying, "Great Sage, please pardon us. We are not monsters, but seven fairy girls sent by Empress Wang to pick peaches and hold the peach banquet. We came to this place and met the soil spirit and other gods, but couldn't find you. We were worried that we might be late for Empress Wang's order, so we decided to pick peaches first, hoping for your pardon." The Great Sage heard their words, changed his anger to joy, and said, "Rise, fairies. Who is being invited to the peach banquet?" The fairy girl replied, "As usual, the banquet is for the Old Buddha from the West, the Bodhisattva, the Arhats, the Avalokiteshvara in the southern polar region, the Saint Emperor from the eastern polar region, the wise men from the five continents and three islands, the Black Emperor from the northern polar region, and the Great Immortal from the center. There are also the Five Zhi Star Lords, the three celestial dignitaries, the four Emperors, and the divine person Ti Taiyi, and the various heavenly deities from the eight palaces and nine halls, as well as the Eighteen Lohans and the immortals of the Heavenly Ridge. This is the gathering of the five flavors and the five Laozi." The Great Sage smiled and said, "Can I also be invited?" The fairy girl replied, "We haven't heard of that." The Great Sage said, "I am the Great Sage of the Heavenly Realm, and why can't I be invited to take a seat? Is there any reason not to?" The fairy girl said, "This is the regulation of the heavenly gathering, I don't know what to do." The Great Sage said, "That's also the case, it's no wonder you don't know. Just wait for a moment, and let me go and ask for some news first, and see if it's possible to invite the old Sun Wukong."

Some, very few, of this sort of houses built at the end of the last century, in these streets of St. Petersburg (in which everything is changing so soon), have remained almost unchanged. Yesterday, upon meeting you, I returned home and came up with one picture. Painters depict Christ by the accounts of the Gospels; I would paint him differently: I would show him alone – his disciples would leave him alone sometimes. I would leave with him only a small child. The child played near him; perhaps he was telling him something in his child's language, Christ was listening, but now he has been lost in thought; his hand involuntarily, absent-mindedly, rested on the child's fair head. He looks off into the distance, into the horizon; a great thought, as vast as the world, rests in his gaze; his face is sad. The child fell silent, leaned against his knees and, propping his elbow against his cheek, raised his head and looked at him pensively, like children sometimes do, stare intently. The sun is setting... That is my picture! You are innocent, and in your innocence lies your perfection. Oh, remember that! What do you care about my passion for you? You're mine now, and I will be by your side for the rest of my life... I will soon die.

The guests turned back along the same wretched path to the house. Nosdrov, leading them, ushered them into his study, where, however, there was no sign of the sort of things one finds in studies, that is to say, books or papers; there were only swords and two rifles – one worth 300 rubles and the other 800 rubles. The son-in-law, having taken a glance around, just shook his head. Then the Turkish daggers were shown to the guests, one of which had the inscription "Master Savelii Sibiria kov" mistakenly carved into it. Next, a hurdy-gurdy appeared before the guests. Nosdrov at once began to turn some sort of something in front of them. The hurdy-gurdy played not without a certain pleasantness, but in the middle, it seemed, something went wrong, because a polonaise ended with a song: "Malbruk rode out to battle", and "Malbruk rode out to battle" unexpectedly ended with some familiar waltz. Long ago Nosdrov had stopped turning the hurdy-gurdy, but in it was one squeaky whistle that was terribly unwilling to quiet down and long continued to squeak. Then tobacco pipes appeared – wooden, clay, cardboard, smoked and unsmoked, covered with string and uncovered, a pipe with a amber mouthpiece, which had just been won in a game, a pouch embroidered by some countess who had fallen head over heels in love with him at a post station, whose fingers, he said, were the most refined superbly – a word that likely meant the highest point of perfection. After snacking on a pickled cabbage roll, they sat down at the table around five o'clock. It was clear that lunch was not the main thing in Nosdrov's life; the dishes did not play a major role: some had been scorched, and some had not been cooked at all. It was clear that the cook was guided by some sort of inspiration and threw in whatever came to hand: if there was chili nearby, he sprinkled chili; if cabbage was nearby, he added cabbage, he added milk, ham, beans – in a word, whatever came to hand, it would be hot, and some taste would come out, probably. Nosdrov laid into the wine, however, before soup had been served, he had already poured guests a full glass of port wine and another of gosternt – because in the provincial and district towns one does not drink plain gosternt. Therefore, Nosdrov ordered a bottle of Madeira to be brought, one better than which the field marshal himself did not drink. The Madeira, indeed, even burned in the mouth, because merchants, knowing the taste of the landowners who loved good Madeira, topped it off recklessly with rum, and sometimes added there imperial vodka, in the hope that Russian stomachs would take it. Then Nosdrov ordered another bottle to be brought, a particular one which, he said, was both Burgundy and Champagne combined. He poured very zealously into both glasses, to the right and to the left, to the son-in-law and Chichikov; Chichikov, however, noticed somehow in passing that he himself had added very little. This made him cautious, and whenever Nosdrov talked or poured a drink for the son-in-law, he at once turned his glass over into the saucer. In a short while, a wild cherry plum cake was brought to the table, which, according to Nosdrov, had an absolutely perfect taste of cream, but which, to their amazement, contained a large amount of raisins. Then they drank some balm, which had a name that was even difficult to remember, and the host himself, in another instance, gave it a different name. Lunch had long since ended, and the wines had been tried, but the guests were still sitting at the table. Chichikov in no way wanted to talk with Nosdrov in front of the son-in-law about the main matter. After all, the son-in-law was a stranger, and the matter required a secluded and friendly conversation. However, the son-in-law was hardly likely to be a man of danger, because he seemed to have stuffed himself enough, and, sitting on a chair, constantly dozed off with his nose. Noticing this himself, he finally began to beg to be let home, but with such a weak and listless voice, as if, in Russian parlance, he was being harnessed to a horse with hobbles.

This person's a scoundrel, and has no sense of self or of others!"

— That's the clincher, you don't know everything, Prince... here... and besides, she's convinced that I'm crazy about her, swear to you, and I, you see, strongly suspect that she loves me too, in her own way, as the saying goes: whom I love, I beat. It seemed to him as if the water was crashing against the wooden walls, as if a roar was rising from the depths of the gangway, like the sound of foaming water, as if the corridor was swaying to the side and as if the waiting parties were being lowered and raised on either side. But the man did not follow the invitation, and instead calmly kept his hands in his pockets and laughed loudly. He who dwells among the heavens fails to recognize the master of the household, and his pride reaches the realm of the sky where the Jian River flows. The Benevolent and Illuminated Holy Sovereign of the Red City, the great hero Erlang, displays his infinite divine might. Upon seeing him, Erlang burst into laughter and, grasping his Golden Iron Whip, shouted, "Who are you, a small warrior from where, that dares to challenge me so boldly?" The Divine Duke exclaimed, "You're an empty-headed fool who can't recognize me! I'm the Jade Emperor's nephew, conferred with the title of Benevolent and Illuminated Holy King Erlang. By Imperial Decree, I have come to seize you, the rebel who has stirred up trouble in the Heavenly Court, advisor to the Heavenly Steed Monkey – you have no inkling of your impending doom!" Erlang said, "I remember the Jade Emperor's daughter, the Goddess of Fortune, descended to the mortal realm and, in collaboration with the Immortal Yang, gave birth to a son who once used an axe to chop down the Peach Mountain – is that you? I would like to berate you several times, but since we have no grudges against each other, I hesitate to strike you down, lest I take your life. As for you, a young noble, you'd best quickly return and summon the Four Heavenly Kings to come out." The Divine Duke upon hearing this grew enraged in his heart and exclaimed, "You impudent monkey! Begone! Let me cut you into pieces!" Erlang dodged the attack by sidestepping and swiftly brandished the Golden Iron Whip, replying in kind. The two of them had a great battle:

His heart high and unyielding, he wouldn't acknowledge the throne as his home, and he dares to reside by the Guang River. Seeing him, he bursts into laughter, smirking, and pulls out his Golden Rope Cudgel, exclaiming loudly: "What kind of insignificant warrior are you, daring to challenge me here?" The Holy Lord roars, "You are blind and foolish, not knowing me! I am the jade Emperor's nephew, and I was officially given the title of Zhēng Huì Líng Wáng. I have been commissioned by Heaven to capture you, the traitor who rebels against the Heavenly Palace. You still don't know when you'll meet your end!" The Great Sage said, "I remember that the jade Emperor's younger sister, Xīfán, descended to the mortal realm, joined forces with Yang, and gave birth to a man who split a mountain with an axe. Is that you? I'll give you a few verbal lashes, but we have no grudge. I pity your life, so I won't strike you down. You young noble, quickly return and call out the four heavenly kings!" The Holy Lord heard this, his heart filled with great anger, and said, "You dirty monkey! Don't be so impudent! I'll cut you with my sword!" The Great Sage dodged to the side, and swiftly raised his Golden Rope Cudgel, parrying with his hand. These two engaged in a fierce battle.

His mind loftier than the heavens, he wouldn't recognize the kindness of his family, his nature as proud as the spirits residing in the Kunlun Mountains. When the Great Saint saw him, he laughed with a grin, drew out his golden rod, and shouted loudly: "You, who are you, a small general, daring to challenge me here?" Today, I am on a mission from above to capture you, a rebellious assistant of the heavenly officers, you still don't know life or death!" The Great Saint said: "I remember the jade emperor's daughter, Si Fen, descending to the world, cooperating with Yang Jun, giving birth to a man, and once using an axe to chop a peach mountain, is that you? I intend to rebuke you a few times, as there's no great grudge between us, but since I'm about to hit you with a rod, it's a pity for your life. You, a young lord, please hastily return and call out the four heavenly kings." The True Lord heard his words and was greatly enraged, saying: "This monkey! Stop being impertinent! Eat my knife!" The Great Saint dodged to the side, and with great speed, lifted his golden rod, hitting back with a swipe of his hand.

"Beat him!" Nоздрев shouted, bursting forward with his wild, curly hairdo, bathed in sweat, like someone storming an impregnable fortress. "Beat him!" he shouted in the same voice that during a great assault he would yell to his squad: "Men, forward!" some sort of daredevil lieutenant, whose brazen bravery had already gained such renown that a special order was given to keep him on a leash during hot business. But the lieutenant had already felt a pre-battle high, everything was spinning around in his head; in front of him was Suvarov, he was storming into a grand deed. "Men, forward!" he shouted, bursting forth, not thinking that he was already harming the carefully thought-out plan of the general assault, that millions of musket barrels were lined up in the embrasures of the impregnable walls, disappearing behind the clouds, that his powerless squad would scatter like chaff in the wind, and that already a fatal bullet was hissing, ready to clap his shrill throat. But if Nоздрев embodied the desperation of the lieutenant who had come storming under the fortress, the fortress he was approaching bore no resemblance to the impregnable one. On the contrary, the fortress felt such fear that its soul was hiding in the very soles of its feet. Already the chair, which he had thought to defend himself with, had been torn from his hands by the fortress guards, already, his eyes closed, alive or dead, he was about to taste the curved dagger of his master, and heaven knows what could have happened to him; but fate saw fit to spare his sides, shoulders, and all the well-bred parts of our hero. Suddenly, unexpectedly, like peals of thunder from the clouds, the metallic sound of a small bell rang out, a clear beat of carriage wheels came from the approaching droshky, and even in the room, the heavy snoring and labored breathing of the overheated horses of the stopped troika were audible. Everyone involuntarily looked out the window: someone, with a mustache, in a half-uniform coat, had climbed out of the droshky. Having inquired at the entrance, he entered at the very moment when Chichikov had not yet recovered from his fright and was in the most pitiful condition that any mortal had ever been in.

— I... you... — he spoke joyfully, — you don't know how I am about you... he's always spoke about you with such enthusiasm, that fellow, Kolya... I love his enthusiasm. I haven't corrupted him! I've only left him... I wanted to leave all of them, all, — but there was no one, no one was there... I wanted to be a doer, I had the right... Oh, how much I wanted! I don't want anything now, I don't want to want anything, I gave myself the word that I won't want anything anymore; let them, let them search for the truth without me! Yes, nature is merciless! Why, — he picked up suddenly with fervor, — why did she, — did she create the most perfect creatures only to mock them afterwards? She made it so that the only creature, which was recognized on earth as perfection... made it so that, after showing it to people, she assigned it the task of saying what it's exactly this that has caused so much bloodshed, that if it had all been spilled at once, people would probably have choked! Oh, it's good that I'm dying! I would probably have said some terrible lie too, nature would have done me that way... I didn't corrupt anyone... I wanted to live for the happiness of all people, for discovery and for proclaiming the truth... I looked out the window at Meyer's wall and I thought for only a quarter of an hour to talk and convince all of them, all of them, but life, if not with people, then with you, somehow came together... and what happened? Nothing! It ended with you despising me! So I'm unnecessary, so I'm a fool, so it's time! And I couldn't even leave a memory! Not a sound, not a trace, not one deed, I couldn't spread a single conviction... Don't laugh at the fool! Forget! Forget everything... please, forget, don't be so cruel! Do you know that, if this tuberculosis hadn't caught me, I would have killed myself...

When the fleeting hours slipped away, lo and behold, it was the seventh day, and Xuanzang once again offered incense before the Tang emperor. At this time, the wonderful news spread throughout the land. Emperor Taizong himself made his grand procession, accompanied by numerous officials, imperial consorts, and relatives, to hurry to the temple. Every person in the city, regardless of age or status, came to the temple to listen to the lectures. There was a bodhisattva and a woodcutter who said to each other, "Today is the Water and Land Assembly, and with a sevenfold multiplication, it will be completed. I and you will mix among the crowd, and I will watch how it will be, and see if the golden cicada will be fortunate enough to wear the treasure I have, and I will also listen to what teaching he will expound." The two of them hurried into the temple.

It was fate that they met old acquaintances; the bodhisattva returned to its original place. Entering the temple, it was truly the Great Tang Dynasty's capital, surpassing the city of Sravasti, rivaling the monastery of Girisha, and not inferior to the temple of Rishabhadatta. The heavenly music resounded, and the Buddhas' names were being chanted. The bodhisattva walked right up to the edge of the multiple treasures platform, and indeed it was the appearance of the enlightened golden cicada.

The poem says:

The ten thousand dharma-dhatus are pure and free of specks, the great dharma master Xuanzang sits high on the platform. Superb birthless souls from the darkness come to listen to the teachings on the bustling market. The skilful actions fit the environment, the spontaneous liberation follows the natural order, and the gates of birth and death open freely. Looking at the exposition of boundless dharma, the young and old alike hold joyful hearts.

The poem says:

Due to meeting with fellow travelers in the dharma assembly, I encountered an old acquaintance who was not ordinary. Talking about the countless things of the present moment, he also discussed the numerous karmic deeds of the dust realm. The dharma-net spreads far and wide across the vast sky, the examined life returns to good thoughts, and the fallen petals of flowers fall like the sky raining down. The dharma-master is on the platform, reciting the "生死救度经" and talking about the "安邦天宝篆," and also expounding the "劝修功卷". The bodhisattva approached the platform, slapped the multiple treasures platform sternly, and shouted loudly, "That monk, you can only talk about the Hinayana teachings, do you know the Mahayana teachings?"

Xuanzang heard this, his heart was overjoyed, and he leapt off the platform, bowed to the bodhisattva, and said, "Respectful father, the disciple has been remiss, incurring great guilt. I have seen all the monks before me expounding the Hinayana teachings, but they do not know the Mahayana teachings." The bodhisattva said, "This Hinayana teaching cannot rescue the dead or bring up the ascended, it can only bring the common people and worldly desires to an end. I have the Mahayana three baskets of Buddha-dharma, which can bring the dead up to heaven, rescue difficult people from suffering, cultivate the dharma-body of boundless lifespan, and create a body that comes and goes without attachment."

Xuanzang (玄奘) raised his finger, then, as if by coincidence, he was invited to speak to the Tang king seven days later. At this time, Xuanzang's merits were widely acknowledged throughout the land. Emperor Taizong left the palace in person, accompanied by numerous officials and members of the imperial family, and arrived early at the temple. People of all ages and ranks from the city gathered to listen to the teaching. There was a bodhisattva and Maudgalyayana who said to each other, "Today is the Water and Land Assembly, the merit of being on this occasion for seven consecutive days will be abundant. I shall mix with the crowd and watch how the assembly will be, and then see if the golden cicada will bring me good fortune in donning my treasure. I shall also listen to which school of teachings will be taught." Both of them went into the temple. Upon entering, they unexpectedly met old acquaintances, Guanyin returned to her original field of practice. They went into the temple to observe and indeed, the great capital of the Tang, was comparable to Sravasti, and far surpassed the preaching grounds of the monastery of Raktamrtikapa. The sublime sound was as clear as a bell, and the Buddha's name was resounded throughout the place. The bodhisattva walked right up to the edge of the Great Treasure Platform, and indeed it was the golden cicada of Maitreya. Poem:

Ten thousand wonders were made manifest and free from stains,
The great Master Xuanzang sat atop the high platform. 
Transmigrating beings from the depths of the underworld come,
To hear the law flowing forth like a market.

Beneficial actions are in response to the workings of the heart,
Emerging from the storehouse, door after door opens.
People listen to the infinite teachings, 
Young and old, all joyful in their hearts.

Another poem:

On a stroll through the preaching hall of the Dharma realm,
I encountered a friend and fellow practitioner.

He talks about the many affairs of the present moment,
And discusses the merits of many eons past.

The Buddha's teachings extend like a banner waving in the wind,
The net of teachings is spread wide, filling the boundless space.

Checking and considering good thoughts of rebirth,
Red flowers falling like autumn rain.

This master of the law, from the high platform, 
Recited the sutra of the Unborn Transcender of Death, 
Expounded the treatise on the Celestial Treasure,
And expounded the scroll of Cultivating Merit.

The bodhisattva stepped forward and with a stern voice called out: "You monk, you only know the small vehicle teachings, do you know the Mahayana teachings?" Xuanzang heard this and greatly rejoiced in his heart, leapt off the platform and saluted the bodhisattva, saying: "Master, your disciple pays respects, numerous transgressions. The monks in front of me all expound the small vehicle teachings, and I do not know the Mahayana teachings." The bodhisattva said, "Your small vehicle teachings cannot save the dead or elevate them, only allowing the mundane and the dusty and the bright to coexist. I possess the Mahayana scriptures in three baskets, capable of saving the dead and elevating them, capable of liberating those in difficulties from suffering, capable of cultivating an immeasurable lifespan, capable of becoming unobstructed and unending."

As time went by, tangling his fingers, the coinciding time arrived, and Xuanzang was again invited to make an offering of incense to the emperor. At that moment, the good news spread far and wide throughout the land. The emperor immediately commanded his carriages to be prepared, and led many officials, empresses, and members of the imperial family to the temple in advance. People of all ages and positions, without exception, hurried to the temple to listen to the lecture. A bodhisattva and Maudgalyayana whispered to each other, "Today is a great water and land assembly; following a seven-day lapse of time, the seventh assembly will be the final one. I and you mix with the crowd, for one reason to see how the assembly will be; for another, to see if the golden cicada can acquire the blessing to wear my treasures; and for the third, to listen to which scriptures and laws he will expound." The two of them entered the temple together. They coincidentally encountered old acquaintances, and Suchness returned to her original dharma realm. Entering the temple to take a look, it was indeed the great capital of the Heavenly Dynasty, surpassing Utpala; it was not inferior to Jetavana; nor was it inferior to Rājagriha. The divine sounds resonated, and the Buddha's name was loudly proclaimed. The bodhisattva went straight to the edge of the Muladhatu platform; it was indeed the physical manifestation of the wise golden cicada. Thereupon it is said:

The ten thousand phenomena are perfectly clear, untainted by the slightest speck of dust; the Great Master Xuanzang sits high on the platform.

The superior and inferior beings' bewildered souls come to hear the law in the midst of a desolate world, and the sound of the law resounds like a city.

The very thing that exists corresponds with the mind's realm, and all manner of things are produced spontaneously, freely entering the realm of the storehouse.

Observing the affairs of life, returning to the thoughts of good deeds, people are delighted, as flowers scattered from heaven rain red petals.

The master was on the platform, reading the "Scripture on Birth and Liberation" for a period, expounding the "Treatise on the Heavenly Treasury" for a period, and expounding the "Treatise on the Practice of Merit" for a period. The bodhisattva approached up close and, slapping the platform with a loud voice, shouted, "That monk only knows how to expound the small vehicle teachings, does he know how to expound the great vehicle?" Xuanzang heard the words and, overjoyed in his heart, flipped over his body, leaped down from the platform, and, bowing his hand, said, "Teacher father, your disciple has not met you, I am guilty of a grave offense. From among the previous crowd of monks, they all lectured on the small vehicle teachings, not knowing the great vehicle teachings." The bodhisattva said, "This small vehicle teaching can only save the deceased and uplift them to heaven, but only allow the worldly and mundane to be enhanced in brightness, while my great vehicle Buddha teaching includes the three canons, which can cause the deceased to ascend to heaven, rescue the difficult people and free them from suffering, cultivate the boundless long-life body, and create a body that has neither coming nor going."

At the time when the sun reached its zenith, Xuanzang again stood up to request to burn incense in the presence of the Tang Emperor. The reputation of the assembly spread far and wide. Emperor Taizong forthwith dismissed the imperial carriage, accompanied by officials of various ranks, and imperial consorts and relatives, to the temple. People of all ages and statuses in the city went to the temple to listen to the teachings. When a Bodhisattva and Moksa were walking, the Bodhisattva said to Moksa, "Today is the Water and Land Assembly, which occurs once every seven years, so this is a satisfactory occasion. I'd like to see how he delivers his teachings and also see if the Golden Cicada puts on my precious treasure and also listen to which sutra he expounds." The two of them followed the crowd into the temple. They just happened to run into old acquaintances, and Bodhisattva returned to his original scripture hall. On entering the temple, the magnificent sights and sounds of the assembly were truly on par with those in heaven and not inferior to those in the realms of Shakya and Rishabhadatta. The melodious dharma sounds resounded through the air, and the cries of the Buddha filled the atmosphere. The Bodhisattva came up to the platform beside the great pagoda, and indeed, the appearance of the Golden Cicada was auspicious and resplendent. Poem: Ten thousand phenomena shine brightly, removing all imperfections, the Great Master Xuanzang sits high on the platform. Transcending ordinary mortal life, the shades of the dead appear in the midst of it all, to hear the law on high. The devotee helps others according to the circumstances, and opens up the doors of rebirth at will. Looking at him expounding the boundless law, the old and the young alike have joy in their hearts. Poem: In the dharma hall of the Dharma realm, meeting a friend from afar is no longer uncommon. Explaining the matters of the present and past, and discussing the merits of many ages, the dharma cloud trails behind like a net covering the entire universe. Checking one's life for good deeds, the flowers of good karma rain down like petals of a blossoming tree. The master on the platform expounds the scripture "Tathagata's Sutra on Rebirth and Nirvana", discusses the scripture "Scripture on Heavenly Treasure", and expounds the scripture "Scripture on Cultivating Merit". The Bodhisattva approached the platform and sternly shouted, "You, that monk, only talks about the teachings of the Lesser Vehicle, can you expound on the teachings of the Great Vehicle?" Upon hearing this, Xuanzang's heart was filled with joy, and he jumped down from the platform. He bowed to the Bodhisattva and said, "Respected teacher, I have committed a great mistake. All the monks I've seen so far have only talked about the teachings of the Lesser Vehicle, but I don't know the teachings of the Great Vehicle." The Bodhisattva replied, "The teachings of the Lesser Vehicle can only save the dead and guide them to the heavens, but can only help the ordinary people and the unenlightened. I have the Three Caskets of the Great Vehicle Buddha dharma, which can transport the dead to the heavens, rescue those in trouble, and liberate beings from suffering, and cultivate a body with infinite lifespan, and attain a state of being unbound and free."

Time slipped away like a palm snapped, but the seventh day coincided with the great assembly, Xuanzang presented incense to the Tang emperor. At this time, the virtuous voice resounded throughout the land. The emperor ascended his throne, accompanied by a multitude of officials, as well as the empress and royal relatives, and hastened to the temple. No matter the high or low-born of the people in the city, all rushed to the temple to listen to the lectures.

As it happened, the bodhisattva and Woodchuck said, "Today is the great assembly of both water and land, with the seventh month followed by the seventh month. I and you are to be mingled among the crowd. First, we will watch how it will be, secondly, we will see whether the cicada king can wear my treasure, and thirdly, we will listen to the teaching of which scriptures he will expound." Both of them threw themselves into the temple.

Upon entering the temple, it was as if they had encountered old acquaintances through good fortune, Bana still returning to its original abode. Upon entering the temple to take a look, it was truly the great capital of the heavenly realm, surpassing the city of Svarga, and not inferior to the heavenly land of Anavatapta. One sound of supernatural music resounded, and the cries of "Buddha" rose and fell.

The bodhisattva went straight to the edge of the Multiplicity Platform, and it was indeed the appearance of the Clear Wisdom Cicada King. There are poems that say:

Ten thousand images are crystal clear and dust-free, the great Master Xuanzang sits on the high platform. The transmigrating soul of beings in the darkness arrives, hearing the teachings that flow on the market square. Causes and effects meet at the opportune moment, and the door of birth and death is opened at will. Looking at the lecturer explaining the uncountable teachings, old and young alike are filled with joy.

There are poems that say:

While strolling through the platform of the dharma world, encountering the familiar is not an ordinary matter. Everything in the present is said to be of the countless affairs, and the merits of many kalpas are discussed. The clouds of the law stretch out and unfold like the group of mountains, and the net of teaching spreads across the boundless space. Counting the thoughts of life as the good path, the red petals of flowers fall like the rain in the sky.

The master on the platform recited one round of the Scripture of Taking Birth and Liberating the Dead, discussed one round of the Treatise on the Heavenly Treasure Script, and announced one round of the Scroll of Encouragement to Cultivate Merit. The bodhisattva approached the platform and shouted loudly, clapping his hands and saying, "You, monk, only know the teachings of the small vehicle, can you expound the teachings of the great vehicle?"

Upon hearing this, Xuanzang's heart was filled with great joy, and he leapt off the platform, getting up to greet the bodhisattva and saying, "Teacher, your disciple fails to pay his respects, and is guilty of many crimes. All the preceding monks only expounded the teachings of the small vehicle, not knowing how to expound the teachings of the great vehicle."

The bodhisattva said, "Your small vehicle teachings can only save the dead from being reborn and elevate them to the heavens, but can only shine on the mundane world. I have the Three Canons of the Great Vehicle teachings, which can elevate the dead to heaven, liberate difficult-to-liberate people from suffering, cultivate boundless lifespan bodies, and create non-coming and non-going."

No sooner had he suffered that complete defeat than, not a word about Nastasya Filipovna was heard from the teacher, either yesterday or today, while he himself was being looked upon as a wonder. The entire family of the teacher, all the girls and children, from fifteen to seven years of age, poured out after their mother and surrounded him, their mouths agape. The teacher's thin, yellowish aunt, wearing a black shawl, stepped out next, and finally the family's grandmother, an elderly woman with spectacles, appeared. The teacher kept begging him to come in and sit down, which the prince did. He immediately understood that they were well aware of who he was and that they were quite aware that yesterday should have been his wedding day, and were dying to ask him about the wedding and the wonder that he was asking them about the one who should now be with him, in Pavlovsk, but they were being discreet. He satisfied their curiosity about the wedding in brief outlines. Amazement, ah's, and shrieks began, to the extent that he was forced to tell almost the rest, of course in main outlines. Finally, the counsel of the wise and worried ladies decided that it was essential to have a word with Rogni and learn from him all about it. If he wasn't at home (which was likely) or wouldn't tell them, they would go to Semenovsky regiment, to a German woman, a friend of Nastasya Filipovna, who lived with her mother: perhaps Nastasya Filipovna, in her agitation and wanting to escape, had stayed with them for the night. The prince stood completely defeated; they afterwards said that he "turned dreadfully pale"; indeed, his legs almost gave way. Through the awful din of voices, he made out that they were deciding to act together with him and asking for his city address. The address he didn't have; they suggested he stop somewhere in a boarding house. The prince thought and gave them the address of his previous boarding house, that very same one where he had had a fit just five days ago. Then he went back to Rogni's.

The news of his defeat had not reached the teacher at all, either the day before or the day of, but all the family, including her numerous brood, from fifteen to seven years old, and her neighbor women, ran out to look at him as if he were a wonder. The teacher asked him to enter and take a seat, which he did. He immediately realized that they all knew who he was and that they were well aware that his wedding was supposed to take place the day before, and that they were dying to ask him both about the wedding and about the wonder that he had come to them, presumably alone. But, being considerate, they restrained themselves. He was brief in answering their curiosity about the wedding. Astonishment, gasps, and screams followed, to the point that he was forced to tell them almost the rest of the story in its main features. Finally, the wise and worried ladies came to the conclusion that it was essential to go to Rogozhin and get information from him firsthand. If he wasn't at home (which was almost certain) or refused to say anything, then they would visit a lady, a German, who was a friend of Nastasya Filippovna's, living with her mother: perhaps Nastasya Filippovna, in her anxiety to escape, had taken refuge with them. The prince got up utterly defeated; they said afterwards that he turned "as white as a ghost"; he was indeed about to faint. Amidst the cacophony of voices, he managed to pick up that they were agreeing to work together with him and were asking him for his city address. He didn't have one handy; they suggested that he stay at a hotel somewhere. The prince thought and gave them the address of his old hotel, the one where he had had an attack just a week ago. Then he set off again to Rogozhin's.

The news of his misfortune had not reached his teacher at all, not yesterday, not today; and on the contrary, they came rushing to look at him as if he were a miracle. The whole large family of his teacher, all the children, from fifteen down to seven years old, poured out in the wake of their mother and surrounded him, with their mouths agape. Behind them came their thin, yellow aunt, wrapped in a black shawl, and finally, the family's grandmother, an old woman in spectacles appeared. The prince got up completely shattered; they said later that he 'looked utterly ashen'; indeed, his legs almost gave way. Then he set off again to see Rogozhin.
